provider.githubDescription: A repository webhook. GitHub tells CraftHub about merged pull requests, reviews and releases.
provider.gitlabDescription: A project webhook. GitLab tells CraftHub about merged merge requests, reviews and releases.
provider.hookDescription: A local hook. Records what your coding agent worked on and uploads it when a session ends.
provider.extractorDescription: The crafthub-extract CLI. Reads local git history on your machine; you review the file before it is uploaded.

kind.mixedExplainer: Mixed activity is held to your work disclosure rules — once the numbers are added together, the safest rule has to win.
kind.bothOption: Both — one machine that holds personal side projects and work repos.

levelSource.role: from the linked role's own level

levelEffect.none: Digests from this connection describe what you built and never name {{employer}}.
levelEffect.summary: Digests from this connection may name {{employer}} and public work, but never internal repositories, codenames, tickets or customers.
levelEffect.full: Digests from this connection carry no CraftHub-side restriction — {{employer}} can be named along with anything else in your profile.

webhook.githubOpen: In the repository, open Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook. You need admin or owner on that repository.
webhook.contentType: Content type: application/json. GitHub defaults to application/x-www-form-urlencoded, which CraftHub cannot verify or read — every delivery would fail.
webhook.githubEvents: Under events, send pull requests, pull request reviews and releases.
webhook.gitlabOpen: In the project, open Settings → Webhooks → Add new webhook. The Maintainer role is enough — you do not need to be the Owner.
webhook.gitlabSecret: Secret token: the value above. Do not click Generate — CraftHub already generated this one and verifies against it.
webhook.gitlabSignature: GitLab 19.0+ signs deliveries with a webhook-signature header. CraftHub prefers that signed path whenever it is present and falls back to the legacy X-Gitlab-Token, so nothing extra is needed either way.
webhook.gitlabTriggers: Under triggers, enable merge request events and releases.

local.hookRecords: The hook records session metadata locally on every turn and uploads it when a session ends — no network calls while you are working.
local.hookPaste: Paste it into ~/.claude/settings.json for every project, or .claude/settings.json for one. If the file already has a "hooks" key, merge the Stop and SessionEnd arrays into it.
local.installCli: Install the CLI first: npm install -g crafthub-extract (or npx crafthub-extract@latest) — the package ships both the crafthub-extract and crafthub-hook binaries.
local.hookConfig: Put this connection's id in ~/.crafthub/extractor.json and a token with the activity:write scope in CRAFTHUB_API_TOKEN, or the hook spools quietly and uploads nothing.
local.runExtract: Run crafthub-extract against your repositories. It reads local git history, writes a JSON file and stops — nothing is uploaded until you run the upload command yourself.
local.extractorConfig: Put this connection's id in ~/.crafthub/extractor.json, and use a token with the activity:write scope, which is not granted by default.
local.reposList: Without a repos list, the extractor only reads the paths you type on the command line.
local.changeCodePath: Change ~/code to the folder your repositories actually live in, then read the file before you trust it.
local.repoScope: Without this, the agent only summarizes the repository it is currently in.
local.yesFlag: --yes skips the review step: the file uploads without you reading it first. Only automate a repo you have already watched a few uploads from.

mcp.plainAsk: Use the CraftHub weekly_update prompt to turn this week's commits into a post.
mcp.claudeDesktopRestart: Fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop — it only reads the config at startup.
mcp.claudeDesktopTools: Open the tools menu in the composer: "crafthub" should be listed with 7 tools.
mcp.claudeDesktopAsk: Ask "list my CraftHub posts" — a token problem shows up here as an "Invalid or expired CraftHub token" error.
mcp.claudeDesktopPrompts: Claude Desktop lists MCP prompts under the + button in the composer, not as slash commands — typing /weekly_update there does nothing. Pick weekly_update, optionally set period / repo / status, and send. Asking in plain language ("write my CraftHub weekly update") works too.
mcp.claudeCodeVerify: Run /mcp inside Claude Code — crafthub should read "connected".
mcp.claudeCodeList: From a shell, claude mcp list prints the same status without opening a session.
mcp.claudeCodeAsk: Ask "list my CraftHub posts" to prove the token works end to end.
mcp.claudeCodePrompts: MCP prompts appear as /mcp__server__prompt — plain /weekly_update will not exist. Add arguments space-separated, e.g. /mcp__crafthub__weekly_update monthly. There is also /mcp__crafthub__since_last_post, which only covers work done since your last CraftHub update.
mcp.cursorVerify: Open Settings → MCP: crafthub should show a green dot and its tool list.
mcp.cursorRed: If it stays red, the args path is wrong — re-run the path command under "Running CraftHub locally?".
mcp.cursorAsk: Ask "list my CraftHub posts" in chat to confirm the token.
mcp.cursorPrompts: Cursor surfaces MCP prompts in the chat / menu on recent versions. If yours doesn't, just ask in plain language — the tool descriptions and the crafthub://guides/post-quality resource carry the same instructions.
mcp.vscodeVerify: Run the MCP: List Servers command — crafthub should be Running.
mcp.vscodeConfirm: VS Code asks for confirmation before starting a server the first time; accept it.
mcp.vscodeAsk: Ask "list my CraftHub posts" in Chat to confirm the token.
mcp.vscodePrompts: VS Code exposes MCP prompts as /mcp.<server>.<prompt> in the Chat view. It will ask you for period, repo and status.
mcp.othersShape: Any MCP-capable agent accepts this shape — put it in the tool's MCP config file (Windsurf: mcp_config.json, Kiro: .kiro/settings/mcp.json, Codex CLI: config.toml's equivalent block).
mcp.othersRestart: Restart the tool, then check its MCP/server list for crafthub.
mcp.othersPrompts: If your tool surfaces MCP prompts, run weekly_update from its prompt picker; if not, the plain-language ask above triggers the same workflow.

token.revokeBody: Any tool using this token will immediately lose access. This cannot be undone.
token.loadFailed: Could not load your tokens. Please try again.
token.allRevoked: No active tokens. Every token on this account has been revoked.
token.empty: You don't have any tokens yet. Create one to let your AI tools post to CraftHub.

settings.advancedHelp: These control what a post is allowed to contain, and the credentials your tools authenticate with. The wizard sets sane defaults — you only need these to change them.
settings.connectSubtitle: Connect your AI coding tools to CraftHub and let them post for you.
settings.automaticPostsSubtitle: Your work becomes a weekly post. Metadata only — never code, never names.

connect.title: Connect your AI coding tools
connect.intro: Connect once and your coding agent learns the whole workflow from CraftHub itself — reading your git history, pulling out what shipped, and writing it up the way a recruiter wants to read it. You never have to paste writing rules into your agent.
connect.tokenNotice: The snippets below are filled in with the token you just created. It is gone when this tab closes — copy the one you need now, or you will have to create another.
connect.replacePlaceholder: Create a token above, then replace {{placeholder}} with it.
connect.whatAgentDoes: What your agent does with your commits
connect.promptShips: The {{promptName}} prompt ships with the server, so the instructions travel with the connection — nothing to paste into your agent, no rules file to maintain. When you run it, your agent reads your git history for the period and pulls out:
connect.houseStyle: The full house style also lives on the server as the <uri>crafthub://guides/post-quality</uri> resource, which your agent can read on its own at any time.
connect.whatShippedDetail: user-visible capabilities, with the ten commits behind one feature collapsed into a single line
connect.impactDetail: who each change helps and how — the part a recruiter reads
connect.realNumbersDetail: latency, bundle size, coverage, endpoints, rows migrated — only ones it can verify in the diff
connect.theStackDetail: named with searchable technology names, read from your dependency and migration diffs
connect.evidenceDetail: a public PR, release or demo, when one exists
connect.scopeAndCountDetail: repo name and how many of your own commits the summary covers, stored as post metadata
connect.employerSafety: What stops your employer's name getting out
connect.profileReadScope: Give the token the profile:read scope so the server can read it — without it your agent assumes the strictest level and will not name any employer at all.
connect.twoPosts: Same week of commits, two very different posts

connections.disconnectBody: CraftHub stops accepting activity from it immediately, and any webhook you configured will start failing. Activity already recorded is kept.
connections.loadFailed: Could not load your activity sources. Please try again.
connections.empty: No activity sources connected yet. Add one to have your work show up without writing the post yourself.
connections.sectionHelp: A connected source turns what you shipped into a periodic digest post. Only hashed, aggregated metadata is stored — never repository names, commit messages or file paths.

connectionDialog.nameHelp: Give this source a name so you can recognize it later.
connectionDialog.saveFailed: Could not save that change. Your previous settings are still in force.
connectionDialog.connectFailed: Could not connect that source. Please try again.
connectionDialog.typeLocked: The source type can't be changed — disconnect and add a new one instead.
connectionDialog.accountLabel: Account or username on that source (optional)
connectionDialog.workExplainer: Work activity belongs to an employer, so it inherits a disclosure level.
connectionDialog.personalExplainer: Personal activity is yours to publish, with no employer to protect.
connectionDialog.bothOption: Both — personal side projects and work repos
connectionDialog.noRolesYet: Add work experience to your profile to link this source to an employer.

connectionDialog.autoPostHelp: Off means digests are still generated on this cadence, but wait for you to approve them.
connectionDialog.agentSummaryToggle: Send the coding agent's own description of each task
connectionDialog.agentSummaryHelp: Off by default. That text is prose a model wrote about what you were working on, and on a work machine it can describe systems, decisions and problems that are your employer's to describe, not yours. Without it, only hashed, aggregated metadata is sent.

createToken.title: Create personal access token
createToken.intro: Tokens let your AI coding tools post to CraftHub on your behalf.
createToken.nameHelp: Give your token a name so you can recognize it later.
createToken.failed: Could not create the token. Please try again.
createToken.copyNow: Copy it now — you won't see it again. This is the only time the full token is shown.
createToken.useAsEnvVar: Use it as CRAFTHUB_API_TOKEN in your AI tool config below. Once you close this dialog it can never be retrieved again — you'll have to create a new one.

scope.profileRead: Read your work history, already redacted to your disclosure level. Without it your agent assumes the strictest level and can't name any employer.
scope.activityWrite: Upload sanitized activity metadata (extractor / Claude hook). Not granted by default.

disclosure.nothingBeyondBlocked: Nothing beyond the blocked terms you add below.
disclosure.intro: Your coding agent can describe what you built without naming who you built it for. CraftHub enforces this on the server: a post that names a blocked employer or client is rejected outright, and the work history your agent can read is redacted before it leaves CraftHub.
disclosure.loadFailed: Could not load your disclosure settings. Please try again.
disclosure.saveFailed: Could not save that change. Your previous setting is still in force.
disclosure.blockedTermsHelp: Words your agent must never publish, whatever the level above — including Full. Client codenames, internal project names, unreleased products. Matching ignores case and only hits whole words, so "Sun" will not redact "sunset".
disclosure.perEmployerHelp: One job at a time. Your open-source role can be Full while a consulting client stays on Summary. Anything left on "Account default" follows the level you picked above.
disclosure.noRoles: Add work experience to your profile to set per-employer rules.

how.title: How automatic posts work
how.yourMachineBody: Git metadata is read locally, by a tool you run. Code never leaves your machine.
how.sanitizerBody: Names are hashed before upload; commit messages are never read at all.
how.crafthubBody: Builds a weekly post from the counts. You approve it before anyone sees it.
how.webhookException: One exception: for GitHub/GitLab webhook sources, the forge POSTs event payloads to CraftHub's server, which extracts the counts and discards the payload — commit messages are never stored. Local sources never send them at all.
how.oneEventVerbatim: One activity event — the entire upload, verbatim
how.timestamps: Timestamps — dates only, so nothing publishes when you sleep
how.badCommitsTitle: Write bad commit messages? Doesn't matter.
how.badCommitsBody: Digest posts never read your commit messages, branch names or file contents. The claims come from events — a change merged, a review submitted, a release shipped — and the technologies come from file types. A repository full of fix stuff produces exactly the same post as a repository full of conventional commits.
how.agentDiffs: Agent-written posts read your actual diffs at writing time, not your messages either. So there is nothing to fill in, no journal to keep and no habit to adopt: the pipeline is built to add zero work to your day.
how.agentSummaryExtra: The one optional extra is the Claude Code hook's agent summary — the agent's own description of the task, capped at 300 characters and off unless you turn it on.
how.catchTitle: Can this hurt you? What's the catch?
how.catchNothingPublishes: Nothing publishes without you. Posts arrive in your review queue and stay there until you approve them, unless you explicitly turn auto-posting on.
how.catchDeletable: Every machine-written post is deletable, and disconnecting a source stops it that second — no notice period, no export.
how.catchBlocked: Employer, client, repository and teammate names are blocked on our servers, not by a promise a model makes. A post naming a blocked term is rejected outright.
how.catchImmutable: Machine posts are immutable once created: you can attach a link, but nobody — not you, not us — can edit the text. That is what makes them worth trusting to a recruiter.
how.catchHonest: The honest catch: work activity on an employer's machine is still their policy call, not ours — see "Why your employer is safe" below.
how.enforcedVsGuidance: What is enforced vs. what is guidance
how.employerSafeBody: For local sources, reading happens on your machine — there is no org OAuth, no app installed on company infrastructure, and nothing for an admin to approve or audit. Webhook sources are the exception: the forge sends event payloads to CraftHub's server, which keeps only the extracted counts. Work sources are held to your disclosure level server-side, and review-before-publish is the default, so nothing goes out unread. One thing we can't do for you: check your company's tooling policy — do that before pointing any of this at a work machine.

setup.secretShownOnce: The signing secret below is shown once and can never be retrieved again. Copy it into your forge now, or you will have to disconnect this source and add it back.
setup.connectedWebhook: This source is connected. {{providerLabel}} sends events to the webhook URL below; the signing secret was shown once when the connection was created. If it never made it into the webhook config, disconnect this source and add it again to get a new one.
setup.connectedLocal: This source is connected. It sends nothing until the local tool below is pointed at it.

safety.enforcedBody: These are checked on our servers. The agent cannot opt out of them, and neither can a leaked token.
safety.enforcedReject: At Summary level, a post naming one of your employers or a term you blocked is rejected before it is saved — the agent gets an error telling it to rewrite.
safety.enforcedRedact: Work history read by the agent is redacted before it leaves CraftHub, so the employer name is never in its context to begin with.
safety.enforcedPolicy: A token can read your policy but never change it. Only you can, from this page.
safety.guidanceTitle: Guidance to the model — not a guarantee
safety.guidanceBody: The server instructs your agent to do these. They are instructions a model follows, so treat them as strong defaults rather than a promise, and read the draft before it goes out.
safety.guidanceStrip: Stripping commit SHAs, branch names, ticket ids, internal service names and file paths.
safety.guidanceSecrets: Not repeating a secret, token or connection string it happens to see in a diff — and telling you it was there.
safety.guidanceDraft: Showing you the draft first, and publishing as a draft when anything is uncertain.
safety.withoutPromptTitle: Without the prompt — a commit log with bullets
safety.withoutPromptBody: Branch names and wip commits. Nothing here tells a reader what the software does or what you're good at.
safety.exampleCommitLog:
- feat: add layout editor
- fix: mobile mirroring bug
- chore: bump deps
- feat(mcp): posts domain + MCP server
- fix: PR #212 review comments
- wip
safety.withPromptTitle: With the prompt — outcome, impact, stack
safety.withPromptBody: Same raw material. Outcomes instead of files, a number you can picture, and a stack a recruiter can search for.
safety.exampleGoodTitle: Shipped a drag-and-drop profile editor with live mobile preview
safety.exampleGoodLead: Spent the week making CraftHub profiles editable without touching code.
safety.exampleGoodBody:
- Built a drag-and-drop layout editor where the desktop and mobile canvases stay mirrored, so a change in one shows up in the other instantly.
- Added direct file uploads for avatars and covers, replacing the paste-a-URL flow that was losing about a third of users at that step.
- Opened the posts API to AI agents over MCP, so a coding assistant can publish an update straight from a terminal.
safety.exampleGoodStack: TypeScript, React 19, Fastify, Drizzle, PostgreSQL. 14 commits.

wizard.title: Add an activity source
wizard.subtitle: Five short steps: pick a source, connect it, watch the first data arrive, read a real preview post, set the rhythm.
wizard.duplicateSource: You already have a {{providerLabel}} ({{kindLabel}}) source. Use Finish setup on that row instead, or disconnect it first.
wizard.scheduleSaveFailed: Could not save the schedule. Your source stays connected — try again.
wizard.noDataYetFine: No data yet is fine — the source keeps listening, and the connection row grows a Finish setup button that reopens this check.
wizard.stepWeeklyRhythm: Weekly rhythm — run weekly_update once a week

source.question: Where does your work happen? Every option sends metadata only — never code, never names.
source.label: Activity source
source.needsPartnerNotice: This source adds context to your posts — it can't start one by itself. A post needs a merged pull request, a submitted review or a release, so combine it with GitHub / GitLab webhooks or the coding agent (MCP).
source.needsDevMachine: Needs your dev machine for setup
source.mcpNoConnection: MCP needs no connection on CraftHub's side — your agent posts with its own token. Nothing to name.
source.workInherits: Work sources inherit your disclosure level — set it under <policyLink>What your agent may share</policyLink>.
source.mcpBody: Works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code + Copilot, Windsurf, Kiro, Codex CLI — anything that speaks MCP. Your agent writes the post itself from your git history; CraftHub adds zero AI cost.
source.mcpReads: Reads: your git history, locally, through your own agent. Never reads: anything server-side — CraftHub only receives the finished post.
source.hookBody: Adds the story of your sessions to your posts, metadata only. It never starts a post on its own — a post needs a merged pull request, a review or a release, so pair it with webhooks or the MCP agent.
source.hookReads: Reads: session metadata when a session ends. Never reads: code, commit messages, file paths.
source.extractorBody: For any machine or repo without an agent; you review a JSON file before anything uploads. It fills in your posts rather than starting them — a post still needs a merged pull request, a review or a release from webhooks or the MCP agent.
source.extractorReads: Reads: local git metadata, hashed on your machine. Never reads: code, branch names, commit messages.
source.webhookBody: Personal repos you own; server-side, no local install.
source.webhookReads: Reads: pushed commits, merged PRs, reviews and releases via webhook. Never reads: your code or the repository contents.

connect.mcpIntro: Two things: a token your agent authenticates with, and a config block for whichever tool you use. The snippets fill in with the token the moment you create it.
connect.webhookIntro: The connection exists on CraftHub's side. Point your forge at it — everything below is prefilled with this connection's real values.
connect.extractorIntro: The extractor reads git metadata locally, writes a file, and stops for your review. Nothing uploads until you say so.
connect.pointCli: Point the CLI at this connection
connect.extractCommand: Extract — reads git metadata, writes crafthub-activity.json, STOPS for your review
connect.uploadCommand: Upload the file you just read
connect.coverEveryProject: Cover every project, not just the one you're in
connect.terminalBuildFolder: Terminal — build it from a projects folder
connect.terminalListRepos: Terminal — list your repos to paste

preview.fixedTemplate: Built from your real activity by a fixed template — no AI, byte-reproducible, nothing here names a repo, employer or teammate.
preview.building: Building your preview from real events…
preview.failedBody: The preview endpoint did not answer. This does not affect the connection — continue, and check the digest from the review queue when it is due.
preview.noActivity: No activity in this window yet
preview.noActivityBody: Your first digest will wait for evidence — silence over filler. Nothing posts until events arrive, so an empty week costs you nothing.
preview.belowBar: Events arrived, but none clears the bar yet
preview.belowBarBody: Digests only make claims they can back: merged pull requests, submitted reviews and releases qualify; a lone commit does not. Keep working — the digest fills itself in.
preview.agentPost: The post your agent just wrote:
preview.agentPostBody: Written by your agent from your git history. It waits in the review queue until you approve it.
preview.noPostYetBody: Run the weekly_update prompt in your agent and the post appears in your review queue — this wizard does not need to be open for that. Nothing is public until you approve it.
preview.windowSummary_one: What your next digest would say — {{count}} event, {{from}} to {{to}}.
preview.windowSummary_other: What your next digest would say — {{count}} events, {{from}} to {{to}}.

verify.listeningBody: Checked every 5 seconds; this flips green the moment the first event lands. To trigger one: {{recoveryGuidance}}
verify.canSkip: You can also skip for now: the connection keeps listening whether this dialog is open or not.
verify.statusFailed: Could not check this connection's status. Still retrying — the connection itself is unaffected.
verify.postDetected: Your agent posted <title>{{postTitle}}</title>. It is in your review queue, not public.
verify.mcpGuidance: Run the weekly_update prompt in your agent now — Claude Code: type /mcp__crafthub__weekly_update; Claude Desktop: + menu → crafthub → weekly_update; other tools: the prompt picker, or just ask for "my CraftHub weekly update". This flips green the moment the post arrives.
verify.mcpRecovery: Check that your agent lists the crafthub server as connected (see the Connect step's verify list), then run the prompt again — in Claude Code it is /mcp__crafthub__weekly_update, not /weekly_update.
verify.hookGuidance: Finish a Claude Code session in a git repo — the hook fires when a session ends, not while you work.
verify.extractorGuidance: Run the extract command against a repo, read the JSON it wrote, then run the upload command.
verify.webhookGuidance: Push a commit or merge a PR in the connected repository, then check the webhook's recent deliveries page for a 2xx response.

token.shownOnce: This token is shown once and never again. The snippets below already contain it — copy them now.
token.heading: Personal access token — shown once
token.uploadsWith: This source uploads with a token ({{scopes}})
token.name: Token name
token.scopeRequirement_one: Fine — use it wherever the snippets below say <token>CRAFTHUB_API_TOKEN</token>. It must carry the <scopes>{{scopes}}</scopes> scope; a token without it is rejected on upload, not silently narrowed.
token.scopeRequirement_other: Fine — use it wherever the snippets below say <token>CRAFTHUB_API_TOKEN</token>. It must carry the <scopes>{{scopes}}</scopes> scopes; a token without them is rejected on upload, not silently narrowed.

schedule.title: Make it automatic
schedule.goalWeekly: The goal: one post a week.
schedule.goalBiweekly: Every two weeks — pair two machines or accounts to alternate and still add up to weekly.
schedule.recommendation: Recommendation: keep auto-posting off until a few digests looked right in the review queue, then flip it on from the connection row.
schedule.promptMonthly: Run the crafthub weekly_update workflow with period monthly and create my post
schedule.promptDefault: Run the crafthub weekly_update workflow and create my post
schedule.claudeRoutines: Recommended — Routines in the Claude Code Desktop app
schedule.claudeRoutinesBody: Routines → New routine → Local, then pick the Weekly preset (day and time) and paste the prompt below. Local routines run sessions on this machine, so they see your local MCP servers — and a run missed while the machine slept fires one catch-up on wake.
schedule.claudePickerLimits: The schedule picker offers Hourly / Daily / Weekdays / Weekly, with no cron box. For {{cadenceNoun}}, ask in chat instead: "every {{cadenceDetail}} at 9am, run my CraftHub update" — Claude creates the task itself.
schedule.cronFallbackBody: The same workflow, headless, on the OS scheduler:
schedule.cronAbsolutePath: Use an absolute path to claude in cron. On macOS prefer launchd — cron skips runs while the machine sleeps; launchd fires missed jobs on wake.
schedule.desktopRecommended: Recommended — schedule it from Claude Code Desktop
schedule.desktopBody: Real scheduling lives in the Claude Code Desktop app: Routines → New routine → Local → Weekly. Local routines reach local MCP servers, so add crafthub to Claude Code as well (the Claude Code tab in the previous step has the one-line command) — the chat app's claude_desktop_config.json is a separate config.
schedule.calendarBody: A {{cadenceNoun}} reminder, then run it by hand from the composer: + menu → crafthub → weekly_update.
schedule.coworkWarning: Cowork's Scheduled tasks are not the tool for this: they run remotely, so they cannot open your repositories or reach a crafthub server running on your machine.
schedule.codexAutomationsBody: Codex → Automations → new {{cadenceNoun}} automation with this prompt:
schedule.codexCronWarning: codex exec in cron currently auto-cancels MCP tool calls unless run with its approvals-bypass flag — prefer the app Automation.
schedule.cursorCron: Recommended — cron + the Cursor agent CLI
schedule.cursorCronBody: The CLI shares the IDE's MCP config, so crafthub is already there, and cron runs it on this machine:
schedule.cursorAutomations: Cursor Automations — only for a hosted setup
schedule.cursorAutomationsBody: Automations schedule prompts in Cursor's cloud sandbox, which cannot reach a crafthub server running on your machine. Use them only if you point CraftHub at a remote API instead.
schedule.copilotCronBody: Copilot's CLI runs the workflow headless on the OS scheduler:
schedule.copilotMcpConfig: Copilot CLI reads MCP servers from ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json — add crafthub there if it only lives in .vscode/mcp.json.
schedule.noCron: No cron on this machine? The universal fallback below covers VS Code too.
schedule.kiroCronBody: Kiro runs headless from cron — pass --trust-tools so the scheduled run can call crafthub without a human at the approval prompt.
schedule.windsurfBody: Windsurf cannot run without its UI — use the universal fallback below.
schedule.biweeklyCron: Plain cron can't express "every two weeks" — keep the weekly schedule (the duplicate guard makes the off-week run a no-op that posts nothing), or use your OS scheduler's own biweekly trigger where it exists (Task Scheduler, launchd).
schedule.noSchedulerTitle: No scheduler at all? The universal fallback
schedule.noSchedulerBody: A repeating calendar reminder plus one minute: open your agent and run the prompt.
schedule.anythingElseHint: Anything else: pick weekly_update from the tool's prompt picker, or just ask for it in plain language.
schedule.duplicateSafe: Every scheduled run is duplicate-safe: the workflow checks your recent posts first and skips if this period is already covered.
schedule.mcpNoConnection: There is no connection to configure on CraftHub's side for MCP — nothing else to save here. Every run's post lands in your review queue pending your approval.

disclosureLevelDescription.summary: Share what you did and how you did it, never who you did it for.
disclosureLevelDescription.detailed: Everything in Summary, plus the companies and public work behind it.
disclosureLevelDescription.full: No CraftHub-side restriction — you decide what the agent may say.

disclosureBullet.dates-and-duration: Start and end dates, and how long each role lasted
disclosureBullet.employment-and-work-model: Employment type (full-time, contract, freelance) and work model (remote, hybrid, on-site)
disclosureBullet.engineering-practices: Engineering practices and strategies (TDD, trunk-based development, event-driven architecture, CI/CD, pair programming)
disclosureBullet.generic-problem-domains: Problem domains described generically (payments, logistics, healthcare scheduling)
disclosureBullet.non-identifying-metrics: Non-identifying outcome metrics ("cut p95 latency 40%", "halved build time")
disclosureBullet.anything-in-profile: Anything present in the profile, work history and posts
disclosureBullet.internal-codenames: Internal repository, service, project and codenames
disclosureBullet.internal-architecture: Internal architecture specifics (topology, vendor contracts, infrastructure layout)
disclosureBullet.employer-identifying-metrics: Any metric that identifies the employer ("the only Brazilian bank processing 4M PIX/day")

search.matchUnavailableDetail: On-device ranking could not run for this search, so results are shown in the search engine's own order.
search.matchCoverage: Covers about {{percent}} of what you searched for — skills, titles and real work history weigh heaviest.

search.promptTip: Tip: you can search with only the text, only the uploaded file, or both.
search.semanticHelp: Used only to improve semantic understanding
search.mandatoryFilters: Required filters — only show candidates who match these (optional)
search.mandatoryFiltersHelp: These are hard requirements, not preferences. Anything you set here removes candidates who don't match — the AI still ranks whoever passes. Leave a field empty to ignore it.
search.mandatoryHelper: Required — candidates must have this to appear
search.selectLocationsPlaceholder: Select multiple locations or type a new one
search.selectLanguagesPlaceholder: Select multiple languages or type a new one
search.yearsRangeInvalid: Min years must be lower or equal to max years
search.salaryRangeInvalid: Min salary must be lower or equal to max salary
search.needsInput: Add text, attach a file, or select at least one filter before searching.
search.noMatchesHelp: No candidates matched this search. Try removing a mandatory filter, widening the years of experience, or describing the role in less specific terms.
search.noResultsYet: No results yet. Write in the chat box or upload a file to start.
search.rerankUnavailable: On-device ranking is unavailable right now, so results are shown in the search engine's own order.
search.matchExplainer: is how much of your search a candidate covers — skills, titles and real work history weigh heaviest. It is not a probability of anything.
search.contactUnavailable: This candidate's contact details are unavailable.
search.aiMatchExplainer: Scores how much of your search each candidate covers, using a small model that runs in your browser.
search.aiMatchPhoneWarning: On a phone it downloads about 1.4 MB and does the maths on your device, which can make it heat up and stop responding. A computer is recommended.
search.aiMatchDefaultOffHere: Off by default here, because this looks like a phone or tablet. Your choice is saved on this device.
search.aiMatchDefaultOnHere: On by default here, because this looks like a computer. Your choice is saved on this device.
search.aiMatchOffNotice: AI Match is off, so candidates keep the search engine's own order and no match percentage is shown. Turn it back on above whenever you want it.

layout.blockKeyboardHelp: {{label}} block. Arrow keys move it, shift plus arrow keys resize it.
layout.dragTheCard: Drag the card to move it
layout.deleteBlockBody: This block will be removed from this viewport layout.
layout.resizeTip: Tip: drag any edge or corner of a block to resize it — make blocks narrower to place them side by side. Blocks always stack to the top, so moving one pushes the others up to fill the space.
layout.tabEmpty: This tab has no blocks yet. Use “Add to tabs section” to place one.
layout.deleteTabBody: The tab is removed from this layout only — the other viewport keeps its own tabs. Blocks inside it move to the first tab of this layout, and pinned blocks are untouched.
layout.tabsEnabledHelp: Tabs let visitors switch between sections of your profile. Turn this off for a single-page profile — only the always-visible section stays on the page. This setting is per view, so you can keep tabs on desktop and turn them off on mobile.
layout.tabsOffNotice: Tabs are off for this view — visitors see only the always-visible section.
layout.tabsHiddenBlocks_one: {{count}} block in the tabs section is only hidden, not deleted. Switch tabs back on to show it again.
layout.tabsHiddenBlocks_other: {{count}} blocks in the tabs section are only hidden, not deleted. Switch tabs back on to show them again.
layout.pinnedHelp: Pinned blocks render above the tab content on every tab.
layout.noPinnedBlocks: No always-visible blocks yet. Use “Add to always-visible” to place one here.
layout.loadErrorBody: Your tabs and blocks are still there — we just couldn't read them right now. Nothing on your profile has changed.
layout.editingViewport: Editing the {{viewportLabel}} layout — desktop and mobile keep their own tabs and arrangement.
layout.pageSubtitle: Design independent layouts for desktop and mobile. Arrange blocks in a freeform grid, group them into content tabs — each viewport has its own — and pin blocks so they show everywhere.
layout.touchArrangeTip: Tip: drag a block by its grip handle to move it, or use the arrows and the plus and minus buttons on each block. Blocks always stack to the top, so moving one pushes the others up to fill the space.
layout.pcLayoutNeedsWiderScreen: The desktop layout is arranged on a 1024px canvas, which does not fit this screen — open the studio on a computer to edit it. It is untouched and still live in the meantime.
layout.previewMobileOnly: Showing the mobile preview. The desktop preview needs a wider screen.
